findings.claim: This test file defines its own hand-written popularTokenBuilder factory instead of using the existing Builder.new<T>().with() pattern, making it inconsistent with the builder style used elsewhere in the test suite.

This test file defines its own hand-written tokenMetadataBuilder that mostly duplicates fields already covered by the existing erc20TokenBuilder in apps/web/src/tests/builders/balances.ts, plus a trusted field, instead of extending or reusing the shared builder pattern.
This test file defines its own hand-written option(overrides) factory instead of using the shared Builder.new<T>().with() pattern used by other builders in the codebase.

The sort comparator converts fiatBalance values with a bare Number(), so a malformed or non-numeric value becomes NaN; since sort treats a NaN comparator result as a tie, this silently skips the fallback sort by symbol, and an empty string is silently coerced to 0 with no signal that the value was invalid.

This file opens with a 16-line comment block covering ticket and acceptance-criteria references, traffic statistics, and verification dates, which goes well beyond the one-line, non-narrative comment style the project expects; the ticket, AC, and traffic context belongs in the PR description instead.

This function has a three-paragraph JSDoc comment citing specific ticket and acceptance-criteria identifiers (WA-3146, #8646, AC C16), which is longer and more narrative than the one-line comment style the project expects; that context belongs in the PR description instead.

This file contains multiple multi-line comment blocks (also at lines 71-76 and 122-124) citing ticket and acceptance-criteria references, which exceeds the one-line, non-narrative comment style the project expects; that context belongs in the PR description instead.

This file has a 4-line comment block that includes a ticket-specific rationale (WA-3150), which is longer than the one-line comment style the project expects; only the reason the code itself cannot show should remain, in a single line.
